Let

\[
u_{ij}=\langle e_i,f_j\rangle .
\]

Then \(U=(u_{ij})\) is a real orthogonal \(3\times 3\) matrix. Multiplying rows by signs does not change the desired product, so we may assume

\[
u_{11}=u_{22}=u_{33}=a\ge 0.
\]

If \(\det U=-1\), replace \(U\) by \(-U\); again the absolute values are unchanged. Thus it is enough to study a rotation matrix \(R\in SO(3)\) whose diagonal entries are equal.

Any non-identity rotation has Rodrigues form

\[
R_{ij}=\cos\theta\,\delta_{ij}+(1-\cos\theta)n_i n_j-\sin\theta\,\varepsilon_{ijk}n_k
\]

for a unit vector \(n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\). Since the diagonal entries are equal,

\[
\cos\theta+(1-\cos\theta)n_1^2
=\cos\theta+(1-\cos\theta)n_2^2
=\cos\theta+(1-\cos\theta)n_3^2.
\]

Unless \(R=I\), this gives

\[
n_1^2=n_2^2=n_3^2=\frac13.
\]

Put \(t=\cos\theta\). Then every diagonal entry equals

\[
d=t+\frac{1-t}{3}=\frac{2t+1}{3}.
\]

For each off-diagonal opposite pair, for example \((R_{12},R_{21})\), we have

\[
|R_{12}R_{21}|
=
\left|\left(\frac{1-t}{3}\right)^2-\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\sqrt3}\right)^2\right|
=
\frac{2(1-t)|2t+1|}{9}.
\]

The three opposite pairs give the same factor, so the full product is

\[
P
=
|d|^3
\left(\frac{2(1-t)|2t+1|}{9}\right)^3
=
\left(\frac{2(1-t)(2t+1)^2}{27}\right)^3.
\]

Now maximize

\[
(1-t)(2t+1)^2,\qquad -1\le t\le 1.
\]

Let \(x=2t+1\), so \(x\in[-1,3]\). Then

\[
(1-t)(2t+1)^2=\frac{(3-x)x^2}{2}.
\]

Its maximum on \([-1,3]\) is \(2\), attained at \(x=-1\) or \(x=2\). Therefore

\[
P_{\max}
=
\left(\frac{2\cdot 2}{27}\right)^3
=
\left(\frac4{27}\right)^3
=
\frac{64}{19683}.
\]

This value is attainable, for instance by the rotation through angle \(\pi\) around the axis \((1,1,1)/\sqrt3\), whose matrix has diagonal entries \(-1/3\) and off-diagonal entries \(2/3\).

\[
\boxed{\frac{64}{19683}}
\]
